name: Ireland
overview: Personal dog and cat travel under the current EU framework, with national arrival procedures and export-certification contacts. Origin group and residence must be confirmed; choosing a departure country does not prove eligibility.

importRequirements.title: Microchip your pet before the rabies vaccination
importRequirements.timing: Before the qualifying rabies vaccination
bullets: Use an ISO 11784/11785-compatible chip, normally a 15-digit number; if it cannot be read by the standard scanner, arrange the permitted reader alternative.
The chip must be implanted or read before the vaccination relied on for travel. On the same day, identification must come first.
Keep the chip number and date on the vaccination and travel documents. An old, clearly readable tattoo made before 3 July 2011 has a narrow exception.

importRequirements.title: Make sure the rabies vaccination is valid
importRequirements.timing: At least 21 days after a first completed vaccination course
bullets: Your pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated against rabies.
A first course needs at least 21 days before it becomes valid for travel. A booster given within the previous dose’s validity does not restart that wait.
Use the valid-from and expiry dates in the vet’s record; protection must still be valid at entry and for any onward journey.

importRequirements.title: Arrange the rabies blood test and waiting period
importRequirements.timing: Sample after the qualifying vaccination; at least 90 days before certificate issue
bullets: For an unlisted-country pathway, use a laboratory approved by the EU and a result of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
For a primary course, sampling is at least 30 days after completion; the current EU rule also provides for sampling within a continuously valid vaccination series.
The sample must be at least 90 days before the animal health certificate is issued. Do not count only to the flight date.
Keep the certified lab report. A documented successful test before leaving the EU may remove the return wait if vaccinations remain continuously valid.

importRequirements.title: Book the official veterinary certificate appointment
importRequirements.timing: Start arranging this several weeks ahead
bullets: Tell the practice the first EU country you will enter and the intended arrival date.
Confirm that an official veterinarian can issue the document, or that the authorised vet’s certificate can receive the required official endorsement.
Bring the chip record, vaccination history and any required blood-test report. Booking early is planning advice, not an extra legal waiting period.

importRequirements.title: Get the Animal Health Certificate issued
importRequirements.timing: Within 10 days before EU entry; issue day counts as day 1
bullets: For a first non-EU entry without a qualifying passport or return-document exception, obtain the official non-commercial animal health certificate. A qualifying existing document may replace a new certificate; GB residents still need an AHC for a new EU trip.
The certificate must cover the first EU entry point. A document signed by an unauthorised practice is not a substitute for official issue or endorsement.
For issue from 1 October 2026, use the new EU model. Onward EU validity is up to six months from the entry check, or rabies expiry if earlier.
Carry the signed non-commercial declaration; an authorised traveller also needs the owner’s written authority and evidence of the owner’s journey within five days.

importRequirements.title: Carry the accepted pet passport or onward travel document
importRequirements.timing: Before departure and at every border check
bullets: For a qualifying EU or passport-equivalent origin, use a valid passport issued by an authorised veterinarian.
Check the recorded chip, owner, rabies valid-from and expiry entries. EU passport issue is tied to the owner’s residence; merely possessing a passport does not prove eligibility.
A valid entry AHC may support onward EU travel within its validity. If vaccination or ownership circumstances have changed, confirm the correct document instead of assuming the old one still works.

importRequirements.title: Have a vet give your dog the required tapeworm treatment
importRequirements.timing: 24 to 120 hours before arrival in Ireland
bullets: A vet must administer a treatment effective against Echinococcus multilocularis, containing praziquantel or an equivalent effective substance.
Have the product, date and exact time recorded and signed in the travel document.
Direct arrival from Norway is exempt within the available country list. A cat does not need this dog-specific treatment.

importRequirements.title: Arrange the Irish arrival compliance check
importRequirements.timing: In advance of arrival, before finalising transport
bullets: Send advance notice and arrange the required compliance check with DAFM.
Use an approved airport or port and confirm that the pet-check service can receive your journey.
An airline reservation does not book the veterinary compliance check, and cargo arrivals need specific handling arrangements.

importRequirements.title: Present your pet and documents at the EU entry check
importRequirements.timing: On arrival at the first EU entry point
bullets: Enter through a designated travellers’ point of entry and present the pet for the identity and document check.
Carry the original certificate, supporting vaccination and test records, and owner declaration; use the customs declaration channel where required.

The ordinary non-commercial framework is for a pet travelling with its owner, or within five days through an authorised person, without sale or transfer. Larger groups have separate rules and exceptions.

exportRequirements.title: Contact the Regional Veterinary Office about export certification
exportRequirements.timing: Before departure; follow the destination’s certificate and permit windows
bullets: For destinations requiring official certification, send the current destination requirements to your Regional Veterinary Office well ahead of travel.
DAFM warns that it may be unable to sign documents without at least two months’ advance contact. Treat this as certification-service lead time, not a universal entry wait.
For qualifying EU travel, arrange an EU pet passport through an authorised vet and keep rabies entries current.

exportRequirements.title: Check the passport before travelling to another EU country
bullets: Use the pet passport or a still-valid entry certificate that supports the onward movement.
Keep the identification and rabies record consistent; the destination may also require a dog-specific tapeworm treatment.
Plan your return before leaving, especially if visiting an unlisted rabies country; a pre-departure antibody test can matter for the return pathway.

originGroups.label: EU or passport-equivalent origin
originGroups.condition: A qualifying passport pathway is available; owner residence, document validity and earlier movements still matter.

originGroups.label: Listed non-EU origin
originGroups.condition: For the qualifying direct pathway, an EU rabies antibody test is not required. The official certificate, chip and valid rabies vaccination remain required; residence and transit can change the pathway.

originGroups.label: Unlisted non-EU origin
originGroups.condition: Plan for an approved rabies antibody test and its waiting period unless a documented return exception applies.

caveats: One personally owned dog or cat; no sale or ownership transfer. Commercial consignments and unusual animal categories require separate handling.
The selected arrival date is not evidence that vaccinations, residence, tests or permits are satisfied.
Norway and Switzerland are passport-equivalent origins for EU entry; this does not make their own import rules identical to the EU.
gaps: DAFM pages were indexed but direct retrieval returned access errors; central EU rules verified independently. Exact arrival portal procedure, fees, current opening hours and cropped-ear conditions remain held.

name: Spain
overview: Personal dog and cat travel under the current EU framework, with national arrival procedures and export-certification contacts. Origin group and residence must be confirmed; choosing a departure country does not prove eligibility.

importRequirements.title: Microchip your pet before the rabies vaccination
importRequirements.timing: Before the qualifying rabies vaccination
bullets: Use an ISO 11784/11785-compatible chip, normally a 15-digit number; if it cannot be read by the standard scanner, arrange the permitted reader alternative.
The chip must be implanted or read before the vaccination relied on for travel. On the same day, identification must come first.
Keep the chip number and date on the vaccination and travel documents. An old, clearly readable tattoo made before 3 July 2011 has a narrow exception.

importRequirements.title: Make sure the rabies vaccination is valid
importRequirements.timing: At least 21 days after a first completed vaccination course
bullets: Your pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated against rabies.
A first course needs at least 21 days before it becomes valid for travel. A booster given within the previous dose’s validity does not restart that wait.
Use the valid-from and expiry dates in the vet’s record; protection must still be valid at entry and for any onward journey.

importRequirements.title: Arrange the rabies blood test and waiting period
importRequirements.timing: Sample after the qualifying vaccination; at least 90 days before certificate issue
bullets: For an unlisted-country pathway, use a laboratory approved by the EU and a result of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
For a primary course, sampling is at least 30 days after completion; the current EU rule also provides for sampling within a continuously valid vaccination series.
The sample must be at least 90 days before the animal health certificate is issued. Do not count only to the flight date.
Keep the certified lab report. A documented successful test before leaving the EU may remove the return wait if vaccinations remain continuously valid.

importRequirements.title: Book the official veterinary certificate appointment
importRequirements.timing: Start arranging this several weeks ahead
bullets: Tell the practice the first EU country you will enter and the intended arrival date.
Confirm that an official veterinarian can issue the document, or that the authorised vet’s certificate can receive the required official endorsement.
Bring the chip record, vaccination history and any required blood-test report. Booking early is planning advice, not an extra legal waiting period.

importRequirements.title: Get the Animal Health Certificate issued
importRequirements.timing: Within 10 days before EU entry; issue day counts as day 1
bullets: For a first non-EU entry without a qualifying passport or return-document exception, obtain the official non-commercial animal health certificate. A qualifying existing document may replace a new certificate; GB residents still need an AHC for a new EU trip.
The certificate must cover the first EU entry point. A document signed by an unauthorised practice is not a substitute for official issue or endorsement.
For issue from 1 October 2026, use the new EU model. Onward EU validity is up to six months from the entry check, or rabies expiry if earlier.
Carry the signed non-commercial declaration; an authorised traveller also needs the owner’s written authority and evidence of the owner’s journey within five days.

importRequirements.title: Carry the accepted pet passport or onward travel document
importRequirements.timing: Before departure and at every border check
bullets: For a qualifying EU or passport-equivalent origin, use a valid passport issued by an authorised veterinarian.
Check the recorded chip, owner, rabies valid-from and expiry entries. EU passport issue is tied to the owner’s residence; merely possessing a passport does not prove eligibility.
A valid entry AHC may support onward EU travel within its validity. If vaccination or ownership circumstances have changed, confirm the correct document instead of assuming the old one still works.

importRequirements.title: Present your pet and documents at the EU entry check
importRequirements.timing: On arrival at the first EU entry point
bullets: Enter through a designated travellers’ point of entry and present the pet for the identity and document check.
Carry the original certificate, supporting vaccination and test records, and owner declaration; use the customs declaration channel where required.

The ordinary non-commercial framework is for a pet travelling with its owner, or within five days through an authorised person, without sale or transfer. Larger groups have separate rules and exceptions.

exportRequirements.title: Ask your vet to arrange the export certificate through CEXGAN
exportRequirements.timing: Before departure; follow the destination’s certificate and permit windows
bullets: Have your vet check the destination-specific export requirements and certificate available through MAPA/CEXGAN.
Complete the required vaccinations, tests and permit application before the final certificate appointment.
For qualifying EU travel, a valid pet passport is the document pathway; a non-EU destination may require separate official certification.

exportRequirements.title: Check the passport before travelling to another EU country
bullets: Use the pet passport or a still-valid entry certificate that supports the onward movement.
Keep the identification and rabies record consistent; the destination may also require a dog-specific tapeworm treatment.
Plan your return before leaving, especially if visiting an unlisted rabies country; a pre-departure antibody test can matter for the return pathway.

originGroups.label: EU or passport-equivalent origin
originGroups.condition: A qualifying passport pathway is available; owner residence, document validity and earlier movements still matter.

originGroups.label: Listed non-EU origin
originGroups.condition: For the qualifying direct pathway, an EU rabies antibody test is not required. The official certificate, chip and valid rabies vaccination remain required; residence and transit can change the pathway.

originGroups.label: Unlisted non-EU origin
originGroups.condition: Plan for an approved rabies antibody test and its waiting period unless a documented return exception applies.

caveats: One personally owned dog or cat; no sale or ownership transfer. Commercial consignments and unusual animal categories require separate handling.
The selected arrival date is not evidence that vaccinations, residence, tests or permits are satisfied.
Norway and Switzerland are passport-equivalent origins for EU entry; this does not make their own import rules identical to the EU.
gaps: MAPA's blood-test text anchors the 90-day wait to entry; the current Commission page anchors it to certificate issue. Use the stricter current certificate-issue anchor pending owner review.
Ceuta, Melilla and breed/local-registration requirements need a separate geographical or local review.
